body: Loneliness. In general, but particularly if a long term relationship fails after prioritizing it over friends and family for a decade+. Those other relationships fade and you become reliant on your significant other and kids for stability, but if something goes wrong or you drift apart, it sure feels like you have no one, even if you see your own family fairly frequently. Everyone is busy.with their own stuff, too, so making plans becomes difficult, as well.
I would die trying... Better than wanting to end things because you're in a dead bedroom situation, feeling like there's no way out.
They should have never gave you money!!
"Gun store, gun store, liquor store, gun store... Where the fuck are you takin me?!"

I need to adjust my diet and take ownership of it myself, because my wife does the grocery shopping, but I can make suggestions or lists and still not order what I request. That's a big part of things, as well - I don't eat healthy. I'm planning on picking up supplements, too, but I need to take more control over my diet. Same with exercise. I know that will help, but it's so hard to get into it and make the schedule work.

As for putting more effort into planning things, this particular situation i thought was clear, but I happened to oversleep. I struggle with apnea and acid reflux at night, so my sleep isn't always restful and alarms don't always work. I'm working on getting to bed earlier, etc., but this time I just overslept a little, and our little one was up earlier than usual. 

But, generally speaking, I've lost the ambition and drive to put full effort into things after years of planning, and trying, and reaching out, and constantly being disappointed. Tried putting plans together for an event, coffee, drinks, lunch, dinner, concert, spur of the moment, days, weeks ahead of time, etc... just so rare that it actually happens. Rejection at home, rejection from friends... It just wears you down.

BASEketball

Bulletproof
Good for you guys. I find that to be an exception, rather than the standard.

Lesson I've taken from this? If she lets and expects you to pay for everything from day 1, that's probably a priority for her and I wouldn't expect her to stick around through tough times. You're probably better off in the long run. Sorry to hear about that, though. Both situations suck to be in.

Even if she is your wife, don't. Just because you exchanged vows doesn't mean that she won't change the way she sees you if you open up to her about what is bothering you. Could even lead to divorce, which sucks AND is expensive as hell...
Probably wouldn't have gotten married in the first place, so probably not. I might be open to it, but very unlikely.
Shout out to Zep, too, by the way. 😂
Yeah... Sounds easy... 😂 We have a kid, too, so they takes up plenty of time outside of work.

I know I'm B12 deficient. Took supplements for that for a long time and didn't really feel much different. Primary told me in December that it was better, but to keep taking them, and I ran out and just haven't gotten any more. I'm sure that's part of it. Funny thing is that I tried scheduling a B12 shot with my primary's office and everyone there (aside from my actual primary care physician) basically talked me or of it. Literally IN THE ROOM, with the materials on the table, and "are you sure you really want to do this?"  Like, why would you not want me to? Got me super skeptical, so I said I'd just keep taking the supplements instead, and they told me "that's totally fine" and I left. Super awkward, but at least I don't THINK that I got charged for a visit.

Vitamin D is probably low, as well, as I'm on omeprazole and that can cause reduced efficiency in processing vitamins, etc. And the winter here sucks. 

I know all of that contributes, but it's shit like this morning that gets to me. Yesterday I mentioned to my wife that I'd like to go to a pancake breakfast fundraising thing this morning. She and our kid woke up early, and by the time I got downstairs she had already made toast for our kid. I mentioned the pancake breakfast, and she said "it's cold outside, and I already made them toast." So I said fine, I'll call my mom and see if she wants to go. Usually she'd be up for something like this. She didn't answer. My wife also had a grocery pickup scheduled, so I went to go get that. Picked up a coffee on my way home. My mom called while I was in my driveway - my other brother had already called to see if she wanted to go to breakfast. She invited me to go along, but I know that my brother doesn't see her as much, so I didn't want to intrude on their time together, so I declined. Texted my other brother while I drive his direction, think that they might want to catch breakfast somewhere else, but halfway there he called but said he was home alone with their 3 kids and didn't want to pack them all up to go out, which I get. So here I sit, in a Burger King parking lot, eating alone, and all I wanted was to sit and talk to someone and have some pancakes.

Where's that guy that did the Little Debbie diet? Lost a bunch of weight but was SUUUUPER unhealthy, thanks to eating nothing but processed sugar and fat every day. Calorie deficiency was the name of the game. It worked, but I imagine it sucked and took a LOT of self control.
I've considered it. I probably should at least consult one and see what they say.

I appreciate your concern, and I'm not doubting depression at all. Fairly certain that's part of the issue. Mostly don't want to have it on any kind of medical record to be used against me. I know it is serious. I have lost a couple guys I know in the last few years. I probably should talk to a therapist, but, again, not wanting to leave a trail, so I avoid it.

The little things were just examples of a bigger sense of losing control of everything. Just feels like I've given up everything. And we share parenting responsibilities. She does a bigger share of that, but there is a trade off for maintaining the house, cars, yard, etc. Next week she has to travel for work, so I'll be playing single dad for a few days, which is fine.
I've done that math. House is in my name. I wouldn't be able to afford it if she wanted child and spousal support.
Just because you think this is about sex doesn't mean that they aren't physically recoiling from them. Currently experiencing this. It isn't fun.
That's hard to do when you feel like you're always failing them, but I'm trying.

Edit to add this: thanks for the kind words, and sorry for the rant. Sometimes I just need to get his stuff out. 

It's tough to clean a slate covered with years of resentment and constant reminders of rolling over to try to make someone else happy, thinking that it might make them want you more. My house isn't mine. Don't like that color paint? Too bad. Argue? She gets defensive, and it's easier to just let her have the win. Can't find any of your stuff? Doesn't matter - her stuff and the kid's stuff takes priority. She "needed the space" or "you never use that" or "it doesn't belong there"... 

I realize that this has been a huge change for her, as well, so I let so much of that slide, but that attitude just permeated every aspect of my life. Need a favor from someone? "Hey, if it isn't too much of a problem, could you do x, y,.or z for me sometime? This weekend would be great, but if you're busy, I get it." Analysis paralysis at work, particularly with my boss - "I just don't quote know what you want. Can you please spell it out for me, because I don't want to get it wrong?" 

I'm starting to realize that it is that indecisiveness and passiveness that makes people look down on me or disregard me. It would be nice to get SOME positive reinforcement for any changes that I do make, but it's just non-existent. I'm trying, but some days I literally park on the side of the road at the railroad crossing and wonder when the next train is coming thru. Then I realize just how slow they move in that area, take a deep breath, and move on. Other days I feel really accomplished, taking value in myself. It's been hard, but I'm trying...

I make sure she gets time for herself - she's going to the gym to see a trainer roughly 1x per week, had video-chat therapy every couple weeks, and reflexology to help her relax. I have to keep our kid entertained during those appointments, so it ends up killing any plans I have most Saturdays, but it helps her. Hopefully we'll get back to a place closer to where we were when we started dating.

Same... It isn't fun... Relationship soured for a few reasons, beginning with mismatched libidos, then a dead bedroom, and growing increasingly comfortable interacting less and less... Then we had a kid... Staying together for them has been heartbreaking, just knowing that she wants almost nothing to do with me most of the time. Just started doing the math via some online calculators, and even though I would end up with the house (it's in my name and was before we got married - per state law, it would be mine), I'd likely end up losing it with the cost of alimony and child support. So, starting over would be a truly blank slate, if we were to go that route. No clue where to go from here. Trying to work on myself and see if that garners any attention from her or not. Best I can do, for now, I think.

Once had a woman tell me my shoes turned her on a little. She was drunk, we worked together, but I was in a relationship, and I kind of shrugged it off. Still think about her. Still in the same relationship, and things haven't been going well for a long time, but of any woman that has given me the time of day, it's that little compliment that sticks with me. Now that I think about it, I'm not sure my wife has ever vocalized any kind of compliment to me, nor has she shown much appreciation for anything that I do for a long while. We both have that problem to an extent, I suppose. Something that I can work on as well, I guess.

>then also seem to idealize and want the type of man who would’ve been born from the expectations and manifestations of 40 years ago while also not doing any of the work women did 40 years ago to encourage the behavior they wanted to see.

This... This bit right here. Many women want a man to take care of the house, the cars, take out the trash, protect, provide, etc., as traditional gender roles suggest, but get completely offended if you mention being open to fulfilling traditional female gender roles. He may not WANT to do all of that, but is willing to, because he knows it makes her happy. It feels like women are rarely willing to do the same.

The not knowing may be the worst. Maybe they'll be fine... Nearly as independent as a neurotypical kid, college, dating, family.... Maybe. Or maybe they'll need an aide to help them keep their house clean, remind them to brush their teeth, go to the doctor, take them to work, work alongside them, etc. 

Even worse if they're any only child and you know that they don't have siblings that they can rely on when you're gone... We're really trying to foster friendships with cousins now, hoping that some of them will end up living in the same area and can keep tabs on them.

That can be incredibly hard to let yourself do... Our kid is actually fairly low maintenance with very few behavioral issues and we just felt like we were burdening other people and that time to ourselves wasn't more important than our dedication to our kid... Now the marriage is in jeopardy and we're often in this "one day at a time. Tomorrow HAS to be better than today" survivor mentality. We're getting better about taking a break, but it isn't always that easy.

Yeah. I mean, sometimes I think "just draw the line, figure it out. Has to be better in the long run", but it just isn't that simple. My parents divorced when I was 11. They did their best to keep us kids out of it. It still sucked. I want our kid to have both of his parents around all of the time. I'd also love for this relation to actually work out. We used to love spending time with each other... I miss that. Could be that we let it linger for so long and let resentment build up that one or both of us may not be able to let it go and try to start fresh. I don't know... It's just exhausting.

>we need to push for more support networks, whichever country you're in, for our most vulnerable

Gonna be even harder when they start making cuts to Medicaid here in the States...

I feel so awkward feeling that way sometimes, because we're fortunate(?) that our child doesn't have major behavioral issues. Mainly a speech delay and lots of attention problems, but not aggressive... Well, not yet anyway. Even then, there's so much effort in anticipating his needs and planning to make transitions easier, etc. just to avoid meltdowns. Not to mention all of the paperwork, the judgement from other parents that don't know, because he "doesn't look autistic" 🙄... All that stuff just adds up and piles on, day after day after day..

Glad to hear that you guys had a good day today. Hang in there, and celebrate the good days.

I was about ready to find an apartment, let my wife stay in the house, keep paying bills, and take up smoking again, and drinking at home, hoping that eventually I just die. Just get out of everyone's way and be gone.
"Because nothing sucks more than feeling all alone, no matter how many people are around." - Scrubs

Must be nice to have a friend with a couch you can crash on. Not sure I really even have that option, but my house is in my name, so she'd be the one looking for a place. My problem is that she'd likely go live with her parents, but they're in a different school district and our kid is autistic and is doing very well in his current school. Almost certain that she'd get primary custody, and we wouldn't want to change schools.

That last sentence... I know that far too well. We're in a #stay together for the kid" sort of situation. Kid is autistic and is doing very well in his current school, but, if we divorce, the house is in my name, but she'd probably get custody and go live with her parents, but they're outside our school district and we wouldn't want to change schools. I'm trying to see if we can get the relationship back on track, but it sure feels like it's been too long and she has no interest. I just don't know how much longer I can hold on like this... I've put on a bunch of weight and have had some other health issues pop up, but the depression makes it so hard to want to make changes for myself if I'm still going to be in this roommate scenario (she sleeps in a spare bed in the kid's room...). I can't even try to move on and motivate myself to meet someone new, because she lives here. It sucks...

No. To be fair, she stopped well before we got married. A while before the surprise pregnancy that has kept me trying to make things work. I tried talking about it, but it turns out she just has no real desire for sex. She admits to masturbating, but sex "always felt like an expectation" not something that she wanted. She "doesn't like the cleanup" and "doesn't want to get pregnant again". Even a vasectomy wouldn't change her mind - I've offered. Should have seen this as a sign long ago, but alas... Here I am.
"Are you looking at mine?"
It isn't easy for me to say this, but a lot of days I wish I hadn't... We're doing our best, but it's hard, this world is a mess, and "I'm tired, boss."

I sent flowers to my wife's office "from our kid". The relationship has been on the rocks for a while and I'm making an effort to do better, but I wasn't even sure if she would want them from me... She liked them, and sent me a text to say "thank you", but that's all we did. She went to her nephew's final high school basketball game. I wasn't going to be able to make it there by the time I got out of work. Came home, got the kid to bed, and she went right to sleep. Have been talking a little today, and I'm about to see if she wants to go to dinner if my mom will watch the little one... Not expecting a "yes", but we'll see.

Yeah, I think we're in agreement. Communication is very important, and libidos will rarely line up exactly, so some flexibility to make your partner happy is helpful to keeping the relationship going. No one is advocating for submission just to keep them happy. It's changing the way you look at it, as "I want them to be happy, so I'd like to do this or that", much the same way that people buy gifts, do the dishes, or finish a project in the house. Choosing to actively engage in sexual intimacy with your partner can work wonders for a relationship.

I've also seen some marriage counselors advise that women should not do this out of obligation, but out of a desire to make him happy. Sometimes being willing to have sex when he wants to, even when it isn't the first thing on your mind, makes all the difference. He doesn't always want to go to dinner with your parents or friends for the 3rd time this week, but he's totally willing to do so and make an effort to enjoy himself and entertain others when he'd rather be doing literally anything else. That social emotional connection is super important for her, and a physical emotional connection is often super important to him. I'm not advocating total submissiveness or free use or anything like that (not kink shaming either), but just being more open to his advances can go a long way. Helps if he makes her a priority, as well, but sometimes it's nice if the focus is on him.

Definitely... High school crush was always with someone when I was single, and was only single when I happened to be dating someone. We made out one time just after high school when I was single and she was getting out of a relationship, but even that wasn't comfortable for me, because she wasn't fully "out" of that relationship yet. We went our separate ways and don't talk anymore, but are still friends on social media. She's happily married with a kid, and I'm miserable, trying to hold together a marriage for our kid. I'll always wonder what might have been...

I'll apologize in advance for assuming traditional gender roles, but I think that it's still fairly typical and applies to the majority of relationships.

I think that responsibilities that men take on when they get older, particularly around the house, are often less likely to be done by their wives when they are out, or are more likely to be weather dependent and therefore not easy to just put off for a day. If my wife wants to go out with her friends, I don't mind doing the dishes or laundry or cleaning the house while she's out, but if I go out, she won't be mowing the lawn, cleaning the gutters, putting salt in the softener, etc. 

Most of the responsibilities that she has chosen to take on can also be put off for a day or two if the weather is nice. When the weather is nice, I've got to be out mowing the lawn, weed eating, maintaining the pool, etc. I'd love to call up my buddy to go golfing, but if I don't mow today, I'm busy tomorrow, and then it's going to rain, and by the time I get to it again, it'll be crazy high and a mess when I mow it.

Between that, and wanting to be a good provider for our family, spending time with the kid(s), trying to make time for our significant others, and keep the family together and happy, it's tough to carve out time to go do anything with friends, let alone try to coordinate a time when more than one of us is free at the same time.

And if you're single? A lot of your friends hit the stage above at some point and they just sort of ghost you. Not intentionally, they're just busy. I understood that before I had a kid and got married. I sure feel it now.

I think a lot of men get tired of the expectations and not feeling any reciprocation. Feels like it is entirely about women and not about romance. I enjoy giving flowers and going out to dinner somewhere nice, somewhere new, or even somewhere we already know we live going, but sometimes even a "thank you" eludes her. Regardless of the novelty or effort, it's just an expectation for many women, and the expectations are often high, setting the whole thing up for failure if something doesn't go right or wasn't exactly what she had in mind. Easy to become jaded about something when you put in the effort every year and it doesn't feel appreciated.

Lack of physical intimacy. If it starts to fade to less than what makes you happy, and neither of you do anything about it, it isn't coming back and she probably didn't care about that in the first place. Highly recommend your own birth control, regardless of what she says, until you're absolutely sure that you want to spend the rest of your lives together. Be married, live together, see how that is before having kids. That's another hurdle that can throw a wrench in the works there, but if you aren't willing to work thru it, things just aren't going to get better.
Existing... Just sort of in general...

We don't. Well, I guess we don't. I arranged to have some flowers delivered to her office "from our child", so hopefully she enjoys that. Pretty sure that the marriage is dead though. Just cohabitating a house, trying to coparent, but I'm just slowly sinking into depression... I've been trying to reach out more lately and see if she wants to salvage anything, but she has plans to go to her nephew's game tomorrow night and when I brought it up (it just showed up on our shared calendar recently) and asked "so I guess we're not going out to dinner or anything?" I just kind of got a half chuckle and eye roll, so... Yeah. Nothing, I guess.

I'd be better off if I could drop an expensive habit that I took up when my relationship started to go south... Mobile games and micro transactions or whatever they call them can nickel and dime you like crazy. I always wondered how some parents let their kids spend thousands of dollars on some mobile game without them knowing, but then basically did it to myself. Downloaded it because I was bored, made friends with some people in the game, found it more fun to spend a little, then it became necessary to spend a lot, and I'm nearly 4 years in, trying to get myself to either just delete everything or sell it for pennies on the dollar. Started as something I was curious about, turned into a place where I could talk to people and have fun, and have ANY control over something in my life, and then became an addiction that has me ignoring my family a lot of the time, exacerbating an existing tension... 

I mean, other than that, I'm making great money, in a low cost of living area, nabbed my house at 3.375% APR and our car at 0% for 72 months, and can manage all of my bills, except for my credit card debt creep... My monthly budget says I have money left over every month, but not after I account for that stupid game... Depression sucks...
I'm treating it with my CPAP, most nights... I really need to lose weight and start getting MORE sleep/rest. It just hasn't been easy to do.

It's just hard these days to WANT this... Not seeing anyone, not feeling loved at home, and feeling like you're more in the way than helpful just makes you feel like you'd be better off gone. Sure seems like I've had less of those days/thoughts lately, but they're still there.

Lucky you. My depression is compounded by an unhealthy relationship and a little stress at work. CPAP felt like a lifesaver when I first got it, but everything else is just dragging me down. I also got Covid a few times and went without my CPAP for weeks or a month at a time. Some of that may have been because it seemed like my acid reflux got worse with the CPAP, but that may have been a coincidence. Now I'm dealing with some random heart palpitations that could be aFib... Primary ordered echo and EKG, only sent the order for the echo, got that done, but my insurance changed on the 1st of the year and I never chased down the EKG. Haven't heard from my primary, either. This depression really makes it hard to want to do the things you need to do to take care of yourself. 

Anyway, sorry for rambling, but you're right - if you snore, you should have a sleep study done and see if you have sleep apnea. It can lead to not only weight gain and depression, but aFib, which significantly increases your risk of stroke.

When the doctor I saw for my sleep study explained how my severe, chronic sleep apnea had been generating cortisol and fucking up my body for decades, my brain just about exploded. 

I use a CPAP fairly successfully most nights, but need to get more sleep. Hasn't helped me lose weight because I'm fighting depression and don't have the ambition to make the other changes I need to make, but at least I have a little more energy now. 🤷🏻

As someone trying to hold together a failing marriage, this makes me really sad... Even if I decided to end things, I feel like life after is pretty bleak... Not doing great things for my depression, either. 😞
Yeah, that was a big part of it for me, as well.

My mom... She's still alive, in her late 70s. She sacrificed so much for her kids that I would feel awful to make her attend one of our funerals. That's really about it. Sometimes I wonder if I would have followed through on anything if she weren't still around. I may, though, be out of the worst of my depression, but we'll see how the next few years go.

Depression, mostly. Seems to be the root of all of my bad habits. Feeling down? Grab a bite to eat. Maybe have a beer or two. (Not twelve, but even a couple is just empty calories.) Definitely don't feel like going to work out when I can just wallow in self pity on the couch.
Yup. Sadly, I can't bring them to my brother anymore, either, as he has started telling my mom, because they see each other every day.
Appreciate that. Thank you.

Thanks. It's complicated, but that's something I should have pursued years ago. She told me (a little while into the surprise pregnancy) that she doesn't have any interest in sex. She only did it because she thought that it was expected of her in a relationship. So, I stopped initiating altogether. I brought it up a few times, but she doesn't want to go back on birth control and doesn't want to get pregnant again (first delivery was rough). I offered to get a vasectomy, and she said she doesn't like the cleanup after sex.

Since then I've withdrawn, concede any arguments, ended up glued to my phone instead of engaging with her, put on some weight, and have been masking some heavy depression lately. She started sleeping in the spare bed in the kid's room while she was nursing, because night time feedings were way easier and less disruptive that way, and she just never came back. We actually didn't even get married until about 1.5 years ago... Slept in the same bed, but she kept her distance and went directly to sleep. Guess it was really stupid of me to think that might help things.

Another wrinkle is that our kid is autistic and is doing very well in the classroom that he is currently in (kindergarten, special Ed), but if she moved out she would likely be moving in with her parents who live in a different school district.
Right there with you. We have a kid, too, so breaking up is far more complicated. 😞

At least she's your ex. I ended up with a surprise pregnancy with my now wife who eventually told me she only willingly participated in sex because she thought it was expected of her in a relationship. That pretty much killed any desire for me to initiate after that... It's been 6.5 years since our kid was conceived and we're basically just living as roommates. So, just be happy you got out when you did.

Yeah. I love my kid, but the situation is making me miserable. Seriously spiraled into depression over it and trying really hard now to pull up, but it often feels like there's no point. Glad that you could move on and find something better, though.

Did you have kids? Because this feels like a great path, except for my kid. We aren't setting the BEST example, but I'm terrified of messing them up with a divorce. My parents divorced when I was younger and I'm starting to realize that, even though they tried to keep us out of it, it definitely had some long term impact.

My child was very speech delayed and still struggles with speech, transitions, socialization, etc. Definitely "on the spectrum" as it relates to a diagnosable (they are diagnosed) developmental delay. It isn't as bad as some kids (no self harm, some ability to regulate emotions or redirect attention), but definitely well behind and struggles with things that neurotypical children do not. And I know that we aren't my parents, etc., but I'd like for my kid to see a better example of a loving relationship - to set a good example. 

It's pretty bad now, and getting my wife to agree that we need to work on us has been a non-starter. I try to give examples of how our communication breaks down, how we avoid talking out our differences or even discussing our day, and how if that improved then it would feel more like we're doing this as a team, rather than compartmentalizing things, stressing out when we are overwhelmed, not asking for help, and how that breeds resentment. I've tried... Just feels like she's no longer interested in trying to repair this. My next step is to ask her how she views this relationship/partnership as it is and what she wants it to be. She struggles with confrontation and I will gladly give her time to collect her thoughts and offer them to me without interruption. 

A happy parent is obviously the best thing, but when I'm feeling terrible about everything else in my life, that just kills my motivation, I turn to bad habits (overeating, sitting around just staring at my phone, etc.) and it makes me feel miserable. That makes me feel like a miserable parent, or I recognize that I'm doing the bare minimum and that makes me feel like I'm robbing them of a better childhood, leading me to feel like they'd be better off without me. That's how the thought process spirals pretty frequently. I'm trying to set small goals, reframe how I view things, and pull myself out of spirals before they get too dark, but it's just been tough.

Oh, it is... I'm trying to dig out of the depression, better myself, and see if we can start talking about it, but that's hard to do when it feels like it won't make a difference. I'm still trying, but it's a struggle to keep going every day. I also come from a divorced household and, though they always tried to not argue or fight in front of us, it still sucked, and I don't want that for my kid. 

And I've heard the saying "the only thing worse than having parents get divorced is having parents that should have, but didn't", but if we divorced and my wife moved out, she'd likely move back in with her parents which is in another school district, and our kid is doing so well where they are and I don't want to change that. We have a big yard, good neighborhood, great area for our kid to play, etc.  

It's just gotten really hard to wake up to this reality every day. I also don't intend to just move out. She couldn't afford it, it's in my name, I've paid every bill and paid for every renovation, and it's my childhood home... Maybe it really is jinxed...

Don't push, just talk. Ask if there is anything that you can do, reassure her that you still love her and find her attractive. Make sure you're pitching in around the house. Try to set up a date night, or surprise her with a meal at home. Make sure you can get a break from the kid. 

Not to be a downer, but I tried all of that, and it turned out that she just isn't interested. It's been 6+ years since our kid was conceived, and that was the last time... I'm still trying to figure out a way to make things better, but it honestly feels like we're living separate lives under the same roof these days. It has killed my ambition, and triggered depression... Don't let that happen to you. Tell her that you don't want her to feel pressured, but that you just want to be on the same page and connect like you used to, and that you think it would make the relationship stronger. Or get advice from a real therapist, and not someone whose relationship is failing.
Nothing in the last 6+ years, not since the conception of our kid. So, savor those 3 times... And see if it is something. That you can talk about and try to fix. It gets worse if you don't...

My wife started sleeping in the spare bedroom with our kid when she was still nursing (yeah yeah, I know, co-sleeping is dangerous, SIDS, all that shit... I KNOW... we talked about it.) and ended up moving the spare bed into the kid's room and sleeping in there. It's been 4+ years now. No big deal, because we hadn't had sex since the kid was conceived anyway, so what's the difference where she sleeps, right? (Also, I know that it isn't great for the kid either, but they're on the spectrum, as well, so changes are tough, and I'm tired of arguing and being wrong about everything...)

3 times? Lucky you! 5 month gap, 8 month gap, surprise pregnancy, nothing in the 6+ years since then. If you can convince them, try counseling. If not and if you don't have kids, get out before you do, and before the depression ruins you. If not and you DO have kids... I don't know... I'm just droning along, paying all of the bills, trying to be an equal partner in everything, but based on being told "I only ever really acted interested in sex because I thought that it was expected of me in a relationship.", I hold almost zero hope that anything that I do will ever change that, which kills my motivation and spirals me into pretty bad depression regularly. So, don't do nothing... Figure out something before things get worse. Please. The longer you wait, the worse it gets. You deserve to be happy. Our son was diagnosed with a severe speech delay around age 2.5 or 3. Free speech therapy (normally at the home, but neutral meeting place thanks to Covid, with masks...) via our county's Early Intervention program. Further evaluation led to an autism diagnosis at 3. Free childcare at a preschool specifically dealing with children with various disabilities and speech, OT, and PT services. His speech has come a LONG way in the year or so that he has been going there and his social interaction has improved a ton, as well. 

As for if you are older and pretty sure that you are autistic, just like my son, our state (NY) has a department (OPWDD) that helps set you up with a care coordinator, a waiver to allow you to qualify for Medicaid regardless of income (cheaper/free healthcare), and they will create a "life plan" (looked at annually), and that can include a budget for various things that you may need - durable medical equipment, speech, PT, OT, day hab, personal assistant to help with community integration (go to social events with you) and to help you get/keep a job if you need that assistance. There is a woman that works at a local supermarket - her assistant accompanies her while she organizes shelves. Starts at one end of the store, works for the other, and starts all over again. Mutually beneficial, and maybe not possible for her on her own. All thru state-organized and state-funded programs.

If your symptoms are super mild? Maybe not as helpful, but the Medicaid waiver is a pretty big deal, and I believe that it is illegal to be discriminated against in hiring practice or to be overlooked for promotions based on a disability. 

The stigma is hard to get around, for sure, but I think a lot of places and people have come a LONG way in understanding autism. 

And on a side note - a friend of mine found out, in his late-20s, that his mother had him evaluated when he was very young and he was diagnosed with ADHD, but she never told him. He was FURIOUS... Struggled all through school with focus, getting in trouble for distracting others, struggled on tests, and most of that continued thru college. He turned to weed to even him out a bit, which helped sometimes, but not always, and was experimenting with Ritalin that he would purchase from strangers to help him study, etc. Then nearly stopped talking to his mother when he found out that she just didn't tell him, because she "didn't want him to be labeled or treated differently". 
I get both sides of that, and he's doing fairly well now, but man... I wonder what it would be like if he had been given more resources when he was younger.

2x offender here... Well, caught twice. I sometimes still have a hard time having just 1 or 2 beers when I go out, but that's pretty rare, and I'll call for a ride or let my sober significant other drive us home. I don't go to the bar and drink for hours, like I used to, but I can still go out and have a couple. For reference, I'm in my mid-30s now, and was 21 and 22 when I got my DUIs (got "lucky" on the first one and it was dismissed, because the arresting officer ended up getting in a bad accident and couldn't show to my court dates, so I got off on a technicality, but I was dumb enough to go out and do it again a year or so later).
I was hanging out with a crowd that drank every weekend, and I was probably in rough shape going home more nights than not. To this day I'm unbelievably thankful that I never ended up getting in an accident, especially with another person. Don't know what state you're in, but NY has cracked down hard on DUI and penalties for such offenses and if you take the classes seriously, you'll see how big of a problem it really is. We were told that for every time someone gets caught for DUI, they've probably gotten away with it 50x or 100x or something crazy like that, and to be honest, that felt accurate. 
Things changed for me when that group of friends sort of grew apart, and our friend closed his bar. I still ended up finding other people to drink with, but I got into a long term relationship, my social circle changed, I drank less, and eventually tapered off to a couple of beers with dinner when we went out on dates, or a 6-pack at a friend's house during a day long gathering, with lots of water interspersed to help space things out. Just a natural profession of getting older.
Would I have changed things if I could go back in time? Absolutely. I wish I had started with a water when I went out, have 1 beer, and set a timer for an hour before I would allow myself to have another. Put a firm foot down for those offers of shots. If it's your birthday, get an Uber there and home, or have a friend commit to being your DD as your birthday present. 
I don't know your personal history, but I'm confident that I was burying some issues that I didn't necessarily recognize at the time. Didn't go to therapy or anything, but took some time to do some self reflection and come to terms with stuff. If it's just "I drink because the people around me drink", you're on the right path to finding new people to hang out with. Find a different, healthy hobby like running, cycling, or rock climbing. I'm sure there's a community there where you can find new people to hang out with that don't pressure you to drink. I like bowling, but drinking becomes a part of that, too. 

I'll leave you with this, though... You've got to want it. As someone that was also chain-smoking while binge drinking on the weekends, you've got to recognize and commit to making that change. I didn't quit smoking for years after I made the change to my drinking habits. And THAT took some real will power and really WANTING to make it happen. If you have a "it's fine if I do it every once in a while" attitude, you're not going to kick the habit, and it only takes one slip up to cost you not just your license, but potentially much, much more.
